programs.name: Homestead Exemption

ratingRequired.quote: any veteran who has been rated by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs or its successor agency pursuant to federal law to have a 100 percent service-connected, permanent, and total disability, and who occupies the real property as his principal place of residence
ratingRequired.note: Add ptRequired: true; a non-permanent 100% rating does not qualify. IU is not mentioned in the statute.

survivingSpouse.quote: The surviving spouse of a veteran eligible for the exemption set forth in this article shall also qualify for the exemption, so long as the death of the veteran occurs on or after January 1, 2011, and the surviving spouse does not remarry. The exemption applies without any restriction on the spouse's moving
survivingSpouse.note: Resolves the brief's lead: as of the 10/21/2026 LIS text the surviving-spouse rules are unchanged (death on/after 1/1/2011, no remarriage, may move). History line ends at 2020 c. 900; no 2026 act is codified.

acreage.correct: at least 1 acre; localities exempting more acreage for elderly/disabled must match it
acreage.quote: if a county, city, or town provides for an exemption from or deferral of real property taxes of more than one acre of land pursuant to Article 2 (§ 58.1-3210 et seq.), then the county, city, or town shall also provide an exemption for the same number of acres

effective date.correct: Exemption starts on the VA rating date (refund of taxes paid after that date, no interest)
effective date.quote: If the veteran's disability rating occurs after January 1, 2011, and he has a qualified primary residence on the date of the rating, then the exemption for him under this section begins on the date of such rating.

programs.effectiveChanges: None. No 2026 session amendment to 58.1-3219.5 appears in the LIS text dated 10/21/2026 (history ends 2020 c. 900). Watch for any constitutional amendment on surviving spouses in the 2026-2027 sessions; none found enacted.
programs.note: Name 'Homestead Exemption' is informal; Virginia calls it the disabled veteran real property tax exemption (Va. Const. art. X, sec. 6-A; Va. Code 58.1-3219.5). type full confirmed.
